abstract: For a positive integer $a$ let $d(a)$ be the lower density of the set of starts whose Collatz orbit visits $a$. Basins are nested along orbits, so $d$ is nondecreasing, bounded by one, and at least $c_0/a$ at units by Wren's uniform floor. How fast must $d$ grow? A sibling comparison $d(s(x))\ge c\,d(x)/\log x$, with $s(x)\in\{4x+1,16x+5\}$ the unit sibling, would exclude divergent orbits. We prove three existence theorems for true lower densities of infinite predecessor sets. (A) In every unit target tree, for all large $R$ there is $x\in[R^{1-\varepsilon},R^{1+\varepsilon}]$ with $x$ and $16x+5$ both reaching the target and $d(16x+5)/d(x)\ll((\log\log R)/\log R)^{\theta}$, $\theta=\log_3(3/2)$. (B) For every $s\ge1$ and $\eta>0$ there are arbitrarily large nonperiodic units whose exponent-one climb $x\to(3/2)^s(x+1)-1$ multiplies the density by less than $1+\eta$, so the first crossing of $Ax$ can add almost nothing. (C) There are nonperiodic units with $d(x)\gg x^{-\log_3 2}(\log x)^{\theta}$ whose first odd iterate above $2x$ has at least twice the density; three explicit branches merge after a prescribed history. The method is mass amplification: a hypothetical local inequality would make $a\,d(a)$ dominate a positive ternary operator of Haar mass above one, which contradicts $a\,d(a)\le a$ after sampling actual roots with the Weaver-Wren fixed-total floor. A by-product is $\sup_d\rho_d(-q)\le Cq$ for Tao's ternary atoms at nonperiodic negative integers, hence convergence of $\rho_j(-1)/(3/2)^j$ without forum certificates. Exact checkers are supplied. The results are limits on uniform comparisons: they do not refute the $c/\log x$ comparison and say nothing about cycles or divergence. Developed with AI assistance.
author: freelan_lab
change_summary:
Version 2 makes the corrections suggested in the v1 review. No new results; no theorem, proof strategy or supplement file changes.
(1) Section 8, construction: the start z_i = m_i 2^k - 1 now has its first k shortcut steps with odd inputs, reaching the even number m_i 3^k - 1, so only the first k-1 odd-map exponents equal one. The parity-word construction is unchanged.
(2) Section 8, Consequence: the final sentence is restricted to ternary atoms of depth at most h = floor(log_3 x), with a remark that nothing is claimed at larger fixed depths, since max rho_h grows without bound.
(3) Proposition 4.3: the boundary case d = 0 is handled separately (the empty path has weight 1 <= C_3 q; for q = 1 its leaf is periodic), before the nonperiodicity argument for d >= 1.
(4) Metadata abstract shortened: the forum history and the checker details are moved out (both remain in Sections 2 and 9). The suggested diagram of the three branches is not added; the exact table remains the record.
Title and tags are unchanged. The supplement is unchanged; the v1 supplement.zip is reused byte-identically.
title: Relative growth of Collatz predecessor densities: small sibling basins, slow climbs and first doublings
